title: Getting to know you: personal questions

objectives.en: Ask and answer basic personal questions: name, origin, age, job.
objectives.es: Hacer y responder preguntas personales básicas: nombre, origen, edad, trabajo.

steps.title: A language exchange at a café

lines.speaker: Martín
lines.text: Yes, I am. Are you Olivia?

lines.speaker: Olivia
lines.text: Yes! Nice to meet you. So, where are you from, Martín?
lines.es: ¡Sí! Mucho gusto. Entonces, ¿de dónde eres, Martín?

lines.speaker: Martín
lines.text: I'm from Uruguay, from Montevideo. And you?
lines.es: Soy de Uruguay, de Montevideo. ¿Y tú?

lines.speaker: Olivia
lines.text: I'm from Ireland. What's your job?
lines.es: Soy de Irlanda. ¿A qué te dedicas?

lines.text: I'm a nurse. What about you?

lines.speaker: Olivia

lines.speaker: Martín

exercises.prompt: Is this their first meeting? (main idea)
Why does Martín say 'Sorry, what's your job again?'

explanation.en: Wh- questions with be use this order: question word + be + subject. What's your name? Where are you from? Who is she? How old are you? Answer with a short sentence and bounce the question back with 'And you?' or 'What about you?'. If you don't understand, say 'Sorry?' or 'Can you say that again, please?' — asking is a communication skill, not a failure.
explanation.es: Las preguntas Wh- con be siguen este orden: palabra interrogativa + be + sujeto. What's your name? Where are you from? Who is she? How old are you? Responde con una frase corta y devuelve la pregunta con «And you?» o «What about you?». Si no entiendes, di «Sorry?» o «Can you say that again, please?»: preguntar es una habilidad comunicativa, no un fracaso.

watchOut.en: Not Spanish word order: 'Where you are from?' ✗ → 'Where are you from?' ✓. 'What is your age?' is correct but formal: people say 'How old are you?'.
watchOut.es: No uses el orden del español: «Where you are from?» ✗ → «Where are you from?» ✓. «What is your age?» es correcto pero formal: se dice «How old are you?».

steps.title: Question intonation and /ɪ/ vs /iː/
steps.focus: Wh- questions usually fall ↘; yes/no questions often rise ↗. Short /ɪ/ vs long /iː/.

tip.en: In Wh- questions (What's your name? ↘) your voice usually goes down at the end; in yes/no questions (Are you a student? ↗) it often goes up. Synthetic voices don't always reproduce intonation well, so exaggerate it yourself when you repeat. For /iː/ (speak, meet) smile slightly and make it long; for /ɪ/ (it, live) relax and keep it short.
tip.es: En las preguntas Wh- (What's your name? ↘) la voz suele bajar al final; en las de sí/no (Are you a student? ↗) suele subir. Las voces sintéticas no siempre reproducen bien la entonación: exagérala tú al repetir. Para /iː/ (speak, meet) sonríe un poco y alárgala; para /ɪ/ (it, live) relaja y hazla corta.

explanation.en: Yes/no questions often rise; Wh- questions usually fall.
explanation.es: Las preguntas de sí/no suelen subir; las Wh- suelen bajar.

challenge.prompt: Interview yourself: ask yourself at least four personal questions aloud (name, origin, job, age, favorite…) and answer each one.

steps.title: Five questions for our new teacher
steps.text:
Five questions for our new teacher!

What's your name?
My name is Richard Okafor, but please call me Rich.

Where are you from?
I'm from Lagos, in Nigeria, but my family is in London now.

How old are you?
I'm forty-one.

What's your favorite word in Spanish?
'Sobremesa'! There isn't one word for it in English.

What languages do you speak?
English, Yoruba, French and a little Spanish.

exercises.prompt: What kind of text is this?
What does the teacher want students to call him?
How many languages does he speak (including a little Spanish)?
